# dtcloud_vm (Data Source)

Looks up a single virtual machine by id.

Lookup is by id because machine names are not unique: the platform holds several machines with the
same name, and its multi-create path generates `name-1`, `name-2` and so on, so a name could not
resolve to one instance.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "dtcloud_vm" "web" {
  id = var.vm_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) ID of the virtual machine to look up.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the VM was created, in RFC 3339 format.
- `flavor_name` (String) Human-readable name of the VM's flavor.
- `image` (String) Name of the image the VM was built from.
- `image_os_type` (String) OS family of the image, e.g. linux or windows.
- `last_modified` (String) When the VM was last modified, in RFC 3339 format.
- `name` (String) Name of the virtual machine.
- `network_interface` (List of Object) Network interfaces currently attached to the VM. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--network_interface))
- `primary_ip` (String) Convenience shortcut: the primary IP of the first public interface, falling back to the first interface with an address.
- `ram` (String) Memory as reported by the API, e.g. "512 MB".
- `ssh_key` (String) Name of the SSH key injected into the VM.
- `status` (String) Current power/provisioning state, e.g. ACTIVE, SHUTOFF, ERROR.
- `task_state` (String) In-flight OpenStack task, empty when the VM is settled.
- `vcpus` (Number) Number of virtual CPUs.
- `volume` (List of Object) Volumes currently attached to the VM, including the boot disk. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--volume))

<a id="nestedatt--network_interface"></a>
### Nested Schema for `network_interface`

Read-Only:

- `is_public` (Boolean)
- `mac_address` (String)
- `network_id` (String)
- `network_name` (String)
- `port_id` (String)
- `primary_ip` (String)
- `secondary_ips` (List of String)
- `security_groups` (List of Object) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedobjatt--network_interface--security_groups))
- `spoofing_protection` (Boolean)

<a id="nestedobjatt--network_interface--security_groups"></a>
### Nested Schema for `network_interface.security_groups`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String)
- `name` (String)



<a id="nestedatt--volume"></a>
### Nested Schema for `volume`

Read-Only:

- `delete_on_termination` (Boolean)
- `id` (String)
- `name` (String)
- `size` (Number)
- `storage_policy` (String)

## Behaviour worth knowing

* **Interfaces and volumes come from their own endpoints**, as on the resource. If one of them cannot
  be read, the lookup still succeeds with a warning and that list stays empty.
* **A machine that does not exist is an error**, not an empty result.
